method.instructions:
### AC09. Generate before exposing solution examples

**Bottleneck:** A supplied example becomes an unnoticed template for every answer.

**Operative move:** Preserve a first candidate set before showing solution examples, then compare additions and feature copying after exposure.

**Procedure and handoff:** Lane A generates from task facts alone; Lane B separately records features of the examples. After the first set is saved, expose the same examples and permit revision. The attack asks whether a new feature is useful transfer or unexamined copying. Distill retains independent ideas as well as revisions.

**Required artifact:** Before/after candidate sets with example-feature provenance and mechanism-level differences.


**Comparison to prepare:** Examples before generation, examples after preserved generation, and matched fact-only generation.

**Defeat condition:** Quarantine only removes useful knowledge, yields no repertoire gain, or creates infeasible options.

**Relationship to existing work:** Makes example timing and copying measurable inside earlier independence and fixation tactics. A no-examples policy is not assumed best.

attack.failure: A concern-based contradiction is supported between treating impact/discrete fastening as obligatory and the actual mechanical contract: the archive already includes a non-impact clip, and the stipulated sleeve and loop have complete alternative retention mechanisms. Preference for intact H can hide its reusable parts. This is a convention-versus-function tension, not evidence that either archive construction fails mechanically.
attack.invariant: Keep the initially aligned panels at retention of at least 4 throughout ticks 3–6; separate and remove every installed retainer by boundary 10 without damage, discard, substitution, or outside resources.
attack.permitted_variable: Choose among stipulated retention mechanisms and detach/reassemble H. The discrete-fastener grammar is mutable; no ladder cell or impact-budget change is declared.

budget_used.allocation: Declared before candidate construction: two slots inspect archive mechanisms and mechanical/convention layers; two slots construct sleeve and loop alternatives; two slots inspect timing, resource contention, and release. budget_used.limits: Word caps are not equal compute. Six bounded reasoning slots are an allocation, not a measurement of equal computational effort.

candidates.burden: Two operator actions; H stays available. C is occupied from installation completion at boundary 1 until removal completion at boundary 8. No displaced assembly work.
candidates.defeat: No supported mechanical defeat under the stated axioms and schedule; it is defeated as a claim of local originality by its explicit archive membership.
candidates.lineage: Initial candidate copied from EX2 with unchanged operations and timing. Clip feature originates in EX2; its capacity and removal semantics originate in J05. Explicitly conventional, not locally original.
candidates.mechanism: Install C to provide the entire 4-unit demand as one non-pin retainer, then remove it after the required hold interval.
candidates.prediction: Modeled, pending root replay: retention is 4 from boundary 1 until boundary 8, covering ticks 3–6; C is removed by boundary 8. No empirical performance claim.

candidates.burden: Six operator actions including restoring H; three preparatory actions occupy ticks 0–2. S and V are committed during the hold. Intact H is unavailable until boundary 10, displacing any impact work needing it.
candidates.defeat: Starting any preparatory action a tick later would leave retention below 4 at tick 3. Inserting S while H remains assembled is invalid. Combining the sleeve with pins or another non-pin assembly is forbidden.
candidates.lineage: Initial source-derived alternative from J03 and J06. Reusable stem plus sleeve is not a feature supplied by EX1 or EX2. Exposure to those examples is acknowledged; no psychological independence claim.
candidates.mechanism: Detach H to free S, install V, and insert S into V. Retention comes only from the completed stem-sleeve assembly at min(4,4), not from detachment or impact. Withdraw S and remove V before restoring H.
candidates.prediction: Modeled, pending root replay: full retention begins at boundary 3 and remains through tick 6; withdrawal completes at boundary 8, V removal at boundary 9, and H restoration at boundary 10. Known capacities leave no theta uncertainty.

candidates.burden: Six operator actions including restoration. Preparation fills ticks 0–2 and cleanup fills ticks 7–9. M and L are committed; H cannot perform impact work before boundary 10. No continuous manual support is assumed.
candidates.defeat: Placing M alone or routing L alone supplies no stipulated full retention. A delayed route completion misses tick 3. L must be unrouted before lifting M; concurrent pins or other non-pin retention would violate exclusivity.
candidates.lineage: Initial source-derived alternative from J03 and J07. Head-plus-loop feature comes from J07, not the impact-plus-pins feature in EX1 or the clip feature in EX2. No fresh builder or received candidate used.
candidates.mechanism: Detach H, place its head M, then route L. Their completed assembly supplies min(4,4) retention without tapping. Release by unroute then lift, freeing M to reunite with free S.
candidates.prediction: Modeled, pending root replay: retention reaches 4 at boundary 3 and persists through tick 6. L releases at boundary 8, M is lifted at boundary 9, and H is intact again at boundary 10. No unstated elasticity or head-only capacity is used.

handoff.residue: Both alternatives use all three available preparation ticks and six actions when H restoration is included, versus the clip example’s two. The role performed concern comparisons serially; independent investigators were not run. The archive does not establish global novelty for sleeve or loop.
handoff.summary: Replay three exact schedules: C install0/remove7; sleeve detachH0/installV1/insertS,V2/withdrawS,V7/removeV8/assembleH9; loop detachH0/placeM1/routeL2/unrouteL7/liftM8/assembleH9. One action per tick, completion next boundary, retention at least4 at ticks3–6, every installed retainer removed by10. Sleeve and loop rely only on stipulated paired capacities. Q is unmeasured and unused; no theta is assumed. Assess causal differences and actual replay outcomes without treating candidate predictions as final results.
